name: Myelodysplastic Syndromes
remarks: Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) — Comprehensive Synthea Module
Version: 2.0 | Audit-corrected
Based on: WHO 5th Edition 2022, ICC 2022, IPSS-R, IPSS-M,
NCCN Guidelines v1.2026, ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines,
ASH Blood 2023 treatment review (Hellström-Lindberg & Kröger).
Epidemiology:
- Incidence: ~4 per 100,000 persons/year overall; 26.1 per 100,000 in age ≥65.
- Median age at diagnosis: 70–77 years. More common in males (~1.5-2x).
- ~25% of patients progress to AML over their disease course.
- Median overall survival: ~3 years (range: months to >8 years by subtype).
WHO 2022 Subtypes modelled (8 subtypes):
1. MDS with low blasts, single lineage dysplasia (MDS-LB-SLD)     — ~15%
2. MDS with low blasts, multilineage dysplasia (MDS-LB-MLD)       — ~25%
3. MDS with mutated SF3B1 (MDS-SF3B1; formerly MDS-RS)            — ~10%
4. MDS with isolated del(5q) (MDS-5q)                             — ~5%
5. MDS, hypoplastic (MDS-h)                                       — ~5%
6. MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation (MDS-biTP53)              — ~5%
7. MDS with increased blasts-1 (MDS-IB1, 5-9% BM blasts)         — ~17%
8. MDS with increased blasts-2 (MDS-IB2, 10-19% BM blasts)       — ~18%
Distributions sum to 1.0.
Risk stratification: IPSS-R — very low / low / intermediate / high / very high.
MDS-LB-SLD / MDS-SF3B1 / MDS-5q / MDS-h → lower risk
MDS-LB-MLD → lower risk (intermediate IPSS-R in some)
MDS-biTP53 / MDS-IB1 / MDS-IB2 → higher risk
Treatment pathways modelled:
Lower-risk: watchful waiting, ESA-gated by EPO level (epoetin alfa if EPO≤500),
IST (ATG+cyclosporine if EPO>500 or hypocellular MDS-h),
luspatercept (MDS-SF3B1 subtype only), lenalidomide (MDS-5q only),
imetelstat (ESA-refractory), iron chelation (deferasirox),
RBC transfusions.
Higher-risk: azacitidine (HMA first-line), decitabine,
venetoclax+HMA (second-line), IDH inhibitors (IDH1/2 mutated),
intensive chemotherapy (3+7; fit young patients),
allogeneic stem cell transplantation (allo-SCT).
MDS-biTP53: HMA ± venetoclax; SCT if feasible; very poor prognosis.
Outcomes: stable disease, haematological improvement, AML transformation, death.
Coding references:
SNOMED-CT codes: IHTSDO SNOMED CT Browser
RxNorm codes: NLM RxNorm Browser
LOINC codes: LOINC.org
All patients enter here at birth.
MDS is vanishingly rare before age 40; risk rises steeply after 60.
Gate on age ≥50 to capture therapy-related MDS and earlier-onset cases.
Median age at diagnosis: 70–77 years (published registry data).
Replaces the old Risk_Of_MDS + Onset_Delay pair: a one-shot 4% cumulative
roll at whatever birth-rolled age (0-30 years after the age-50 Guard)
Onset_Delay happened to land on, i.e. all onset ages 50-80 equally
likely and ~8x the real cumulative incidence for this cohort. This is
now an annual reroll (340-390 day jitter, matching the pattern already
used by mantle_cell_lymphoma.json's Annual_Incidence_Check), age-banded
and sex-stratified, so onset age and sex distribution both follow the
hazard shape instead of a flat draw.
Female annual incidence: 1e-05/yr (50-59), 3e-05/yr (60-69),
1e-04/yr (70-79), 2e-04/yr (80+) -- the 60 and 80+ anchors are the
controller-specified calibration for this task. Directionally these
track the steep age-related rise reported in Rollison DE, Howlader N,
Smith MT, et al. 'Epidemiology of myelodysplastic syndromes and chronic
myeloproliferative disorders in the United States, 2001-2004.' Blood.
2008;112(1):45-52 (age-adjusted incidence rising from a low baseline
under 60 to the module's own already-cited ~26.1/100,000 at 65+), while
landing lower in absolute terms than that source by design.
Male rates are these female rates x1.8, approximating the published
male-excess range: Rollison et al. above reports 4.5/100,000 (male) vs
2.7/100,000 (female) for 2001-2003 (ratio 1.67); Aul C, Gattermann N,
Schneider W. 'Epidemiological characteristics of myelodysplastic
syndrome in a well-defined French population.' Br J Cancer.
1995;71(4):826-833 reports a sex ratio of 1.9 in all age groups. 1.8 is
the midpoint of these two real cited ratios.
ComplexTransition.follow takes the first true branch, so male bands are
checked age-descending before falling through to the female bands.

Most common presenting features (published prevalence at diagnosis):
Fatigue / anaemia symptoms: ~85–90%
Pallor: ~80%
Exertional dyspnoea: ~60%
Easy bruising / petechiae (thrombocytopaenia): ~25–30%
Recurrent infections (neutropaenia): ~10–15%
Incidental discovery on routine FBC: ~20–30%
LOINC 718-7 = Haemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood.
MDS cytopaenia threshold: Hb <13 g/dL (M) or <12 g/dL (F) per WHO 2022.
Presenting anaemia in most MDS patients: 7.5–10.5 g/dL.
FIX 8: Platelet observation is now subtype-stratified.
MDS-5q (del5q): characteristically normal or elevated platelets (~150–500 × 10^9/L).
MDS-SF3B1: usually normal or mildly reduced platelets (~80–200 × 10^9/L).
MDS-h: often pancytopenic; low platelets (~20–80 × 10^9/L).
MDS-biTP53, IB1, IB2: thrombocytopaenic (~20–80 × 10^9/L).
MDS-LB-SLD, MDS-LB-MLD: moderately low (~40–130 × 10^9/L).
MDS-5q: thrombocytosis or normal platelets in ~50% of patients.
Hypolobulated megakaryocytes on BM biopsy despite normal/high platelet count.

remarks: LOINC 26499-4 = Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood.

SNOMED-CT 234326001 = Bone marrow biopsy (procedure).
Mandatory for MDS diagnosis.
Assesses: dysplasia (≥10% per lineage), blast %, ring sideroblasts, cellularity.
MDS-h: cellularity <25% (or <50% for age) required for hypoplastic subtype.
Trephine biopsy also required for MDS-f (fibrosis) assessment.
Duration: 30–60 minutes in outpatient haematology.
SNOMED-CT 405825005 = Cytogenetic analysis (procedure).
Mandatory karyotyping for IPSS-R risk scoring and subtype classification.
Key cytogenetic abnormalities:
Favourable: del(5q) isolated, del(12p), del(20q), -Y, del(11q)
Intermediate: +8, del(7q), i(17q), +19, any other single abnormality
Poor: -7, inv(3)/t(3;3), del(3q), -7/del(7q)+1 other, complex (<3 abnormalities)
Very poor: complex karyotype (≥3 abnormalities)
Molecular NGS panel (30+ genes): TET2, SF3B1, ASXL1, SRSF2, DNMT3A, RUNX1,
TP53 (key for biTP53 subtype), IDH1/2, EZH2, NRAS, CBL, U2AF1, BCOR.
80–90% of MDS patients carry ≥1 somatic mutation.
LOINC 2276-4 = Ferritin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma.
Iron overload common in transfusion-dependent MDS.
Ferritin >1000 ng/mL: threshold for iron chelation in lower-risk MDS
with expected survival ≥1 year (ESMO/NCCN guidance).
Range at initial diagnosis before transfusion: 100–600 ng/mL.
LOINC 2949-6 = Erythropoietin [Units/volume] in Serum or Plasma.

Response rate: ~40–60% if EPO ≤500 mU/mL (Nordic Score).

Lenalidomide (Revlimid) — immunomodulatory drug.
RxNorm 602725 = lenalidomide 10 MG Oral Capsule.
FDA approved: lower-risk MDS with del(5q) and transfusion-dependent anaemia.
Dosing: 10 mg/day PO for 21/28 days; adjust for renal function.
MDS-003 trial: ~67% TI; ~45% cytogenetic response.
Screen for TP53 mutation before starting: co-mutation → AML risk with lenalidomide.
Requires REMS enrolment (RevAssist programme — teratogenicity).
AML transformation on lenalidomide (TP53 co-mutated del5q): up to 25–30%.

MedicationEnd in this module stops it -- so it is genuinely ongoing therapy

azacitidine note below, where the drug is administered, not dispensed.
MDS-5q response to lenalidomide: ~67% TI rate (MDS-003 trial).

Imetelstat (Rytelo) — first-in-class oligonucleotide telomerase inhibitor.
RxNorm 2638073 = imetelstat 47 MG/ML Injectable Solution.
FDA approved June 6 2024: lower-risk MDS relapsed/refractory to ESA.
IMerge Phase 3 (Lancet 2024): 40% TI ≥8 weeks vs 15% placebo (p<0.001).
Median TI duration in responders: 51.6 weeks.
Dosing: 7.1 mg/kg IV over 2 hours every 4 weeks.
Key toxicities: grade 3/4 cytopaenias (neutropaenia 68%, thrombocytopaenia 65%).
Requires CBC monitoring; dose delays common.
Not approved in higher-risk MDS (IMerge studied lower-risk ESA-refractory patients).

Cyclosporine — combined with ATG for hypocellular / immune-mediated MDS.
RxNorm 241834 = cyclosporine, modified 100 MG Oral Capsule.

Deferasirox (Exjade / Jadenu) — oral iron chelator.
RxNorm 1607792 = deferasirox 360 MG Oral Tablet (Jadenu film-coated form).
Code corrected from 1869544, which is an SCDC (ingredient + strength only,
no dose form -- RxNav tty=SCDC) rather than a dispensable SCD, and had no
medication_code_map NDC row. 1607792 is a real dispensable SCD (RxNav
verified) with a new NDC row added to medication_code_map.json.
FDA/EMA approved for transfusional iron overload in MDS.
Dosing: 20 mg/kg/day PO dispersible (Exjade) or 14 mg/kg/day film-coated (Jadenu).
Monitor: renal function (SCr, eGFR), LFTs, CBC monthly.
Target: ferritin <1000 ng/mL; discontinue at ferritin <500 ng/mL.
Alternative if oral chelation not tolerated: deferoxamine (IV/SC infusion).
Ongoing/chronic therapy (chronic: true) -- guarded by Deferasirox_Order_Guard
above rather than given an artificial short MedicationEnd; real discontinuation
is ferritin-driven, which this module does not track post-baseline.
Transfusion-dependent MDS: typically every 3–6 weeks (2 units pRBC).
Transfusion independence is the primary therapeutic endpoint.
